findings.text: follow-on: test_a_worker_that_ends_on_the_stop_ends_the_supervisor_promptly asserts a raw wall-clock elapsed <= PROMPT_BOUND_SECONDS (= 2*poll + slack = 14s) with no tolerance, so it is load-flaky. In the node's own negative-control log (logs/negative_control.log) this case failed with 'assert 16.734441246837378 <= 14.0' even though the mutation it is meant to be insensitive to (a 600s stop grace) cannot affect a worker that ends on the group stop - the extra seconds are machine load. I re-ran the same case under the same mutation in a scratch tree and it passed (review-logs/review-negative-control.log). Because this case is in the gate file, a loaded node can redden the node's own 2-passed gate for a reason unrelated to the change. The bound test (test_the_supervisor_exits_within_the_bound_after_a_stop) is not exposed this way: it waits up to BOUND+5 and only then compares elapsed, so its assertion is reachable without the wait itself failing on load. Fix direction: give the prompt case the same SIGKILL-safety or a generous slack, or derive its expectation from the poll the supervisor actually paid rather than a fixed 14s.

follow-on: The negative-control log's recorded command header is 'pytest -m no:cacheprovider', but -m is a marker expression, not the cache flag: on the project venv it deselects every test ('2 deselected (2 selected)' via --collect-only), so the stated command cannot produce the log's own 'FF ... 2 failed EXIT=1' body. The correct flag (-p no:cacheprovider) is used in gate.log, base_arm.log and head_arm.log, so this is a mistyped header on the admission-bearing artifact: a reader cannot reproduce the negative control from the command the log names. The substance still holds - I reproduced the mutation with the correct flag (1 failed, EXIT=1) - but the log should name the command that actually ran.

justifications.durability: The guard lives in product source and the docstring states the mechanism (a stop is already delivered to the worker; the grace only covers the flush between receiving it and exiting). It is attributable: the SIGKILL path calls signal_worker with reason worker-ignored-the-stop-grace-signal into the run's sender record, which the test asserts. The covering test fails when the escalation is withheld, reproduced by me (negative control EXIT=1 on the bound case). Weaker points: (a) the positive-control case test_a_worker_that_ends_on_the_stop_ends_the_supervisor_promptly asserts a raw wall-clock elapsed <= PROMPT_BOUND_SECONDS with no tolerance, and it is load-flaky - it failed at 16.73s > 14s in the author's own negative-control run and passed in mine, so the gate can spuriously redden on a loaded node (see finding); (b) the production default (10s) is not exercised by any case, since both cases set the grace to 1s via the env.

Both arm logs carry the three named test files with module and cwd headers: base e89a94bde 16 passed EXIT=0 (logs/base_arm.log), head e1f64d7a7 16 passed EXIT=0 (logs/head_arm.log); both failure_count 0, so the manifest's added_failure_count of 0 is well-founded. I independently reproduced in a scratch tree extracted from the reviewed worktree (PYTHONPATH=/tmp/.../rev-head-yv0k): the new file 2 passed EXIT=0 (review-logs/review-head-rerun.log), and the declared mutation RECKON_STOP_SUPERVISOR_NEGATIVE_CONTROL=wait reddens the bound case (review-logs/review-negative-control.log, EXIT=1). Deducted for two provenance defects in the evidence: (1) the negative-control log's own command header records 'pytest -m no:cacheprovider' (logs/negative_control.log line 3), and -m is a marker filter: on this venv it deselects every test ('2 deselected' on --collect-only), so the stated command cannot have produced the log's own 'FF' output; the correct flag (-p) is used in gate.log, base_arm.log and head_arm.log, so the negative-control header is mistyped and does not name what ran; (2) the manifest quotes a hand-authored reproduction (15.4s unbounded vs 3.3s) that is not backed by any log on disk.
justifications.fit: The change sits where the grace machinery already lives: STOP_GRACE_ENV and STOP_GRACE_DEFAULT sit beside _WORKER_GRACE_KILL_SECONDS, and the new helper _stop_grace_seconds() is a sibling of _terminal_manifest_grace_seconds(), reading touch the same env idiom and floor at zero. The two new keyword parameters thread cleanly onto the existing single caller. The env override exists so a test can shorten the grace, matching the pre-existing terminal-manifest grace pattern rather than inventing a parallel one. Names read as what the code does (stop_grace_seconds, worker-ignored-the-stop-grace-signal, run-stop). No version suffixes, no plan/sprint/ticket identifiers in symbols or comments, no AI attribution. The test module's docstring states the mechanism (the supervisor blocks in waitpid) rather than a ticket id.
justifications.goal_fidelity: The done-when is met. The reported defect was a supervisor still alive ~45s after crew stop (r-20261002T052254559858): the supervisor's SIGTERM handler only records the stop and then blocks in os.waitpid for as long as the worker lives, so a worker that ignores the group stop holds the supervisor, and its slot, unbounded. The fix bounds that wait: _reap_worker_on_its_terminal_manifest (reckon/crew/dispatch.py:8566+) now takes stop_requested and stop_grace_seconds, and once the stop flag is set it re-signals the worker with reason run-stop, then SIGKILLs it with reason worker-ignored-the-stop-grace-signal after the grace (dispatch.py:8610-8631). The stop flag is the supervisor's own handler event (_record_stop_before_spawn, dispatch.py:8311), which fires because crew stop -> terminate() signals the worker's whole process group (_signal_process_group, dispatch.py:10287). The bound the node states is the existing 3s reap poll plus the configured stop grace plus the exit-record write; STOP_GRACE_DEFAULT is the pre-existing 10s _WORKER_GRACE_KILL_SECONDS and is overridable via RECKON_WORKER_STOP_GRACE_SECONDS. The test asserts the supervisor's pid is gone within the bound and that the escalation is attributable in the run's own sender record. Names what it waits on: the worker's exit (docstring lines 3-8), reproduced by the node's own unbounded 15.4s observation quoted in the manifest.
justifications.scope_discipline: The base..HEAD diff is confined to the node's declared write paths and nothing else: reckon/crew/dispatch.py (+67/-1) and tests/test_a_stopped_run_ends_its_supervisor.py (+292, new), 358 insertions/1 deletion across exactly two files. No plan HTML is edited; no ledger, index or sprint state is touched; the manifest's changed_paths names the same two files. git status in the reviewed worktree is clean at e1f64d7a7. The node also declared docs/evidence/fragments/.../a-stopped-run-ends-its-supervisor.html and a docs/figures directory and emitted neither; that is an under-delivery, not a scope breach, and the done-when names only the test artifact, so it is not counted against discipline.
